application_context.summary: Synthetic CRM MERGE of CRM-ACCT-2097 into canonical CRM-ACCT-1042 (planning exercise only). Three separate determinations: (1) Identity continuity - the supplied descriptions SUPPORT the proposition that both records denote one continuing legal person (registry ID FIC-REG-004821; legal-name change effective 2024-04-01), conditional on authenticity and customer-policy eligibility; the evidence is not verified by the Planner and is not yet authorization-eligible. (2) Human review - the proposition, evidence analysis and operation scope are specific enough for Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner review; review is not approval. (3) Commit authorization - NOT authorized: no approval artifacts exist, write-set completeness and atomicity are unverified, and the authorization path (Path A or Path B) is unresolved; the design-time decision is HOLD.
application_context.temporal_scope: Legal-name change effective 2024-04-01; registry extract dated 2026-10-15; continuity must hold from creation of CRM-ACCT-1042 (2019-06-12) through the commit time; evidence currency window not defined by policy
application_context.persistence_mechanism: Customer requirement: one PostgreSQL 16.5 SERIALIZABLE transaction covering all database writes and the outbox insertion, with asynchronous outbox consumers after commit (declared; not verified)

operations.title: Merge CRM-ACCT-2097 into canonical CRM-ACCT-1042
operations.identity_proposition: CRM-ACCT-2097 (Northstar Industrial Components Limited) and CRM-ACCT-1042 (Northstar Components Ltd.; legacy legal name Northstar Components Limited) denote the same continuing legal person identified by official registry ID FIC-REG-004821, whose legal name changed on 2024-04-01 without change of registration number or legal-person continuity, so that CRM-ACCT-2097 may be merged into canonical CRM-ACCT-1042 under POL-MDM-07 v3.2.
affected_state: UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: accounts - customer-declared write-set member (canonical row CRM-ACCT-1042 at row version 18; source row CRM-ACCT-2097 at row version 23); membership in one SERIALIZABLE transaction is a customer requirement and is not verified by implementation evidence

UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: account_contact_links - customer-declared write-set member (three links on CRM-ACCT-2097, four on CRM-ACCT-1042); duplicate-contact handling and transaction membership not verified
UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: account_contract_links - customer-declared write-set member (two active contracts on CRM-ACCT-2097, six on CRM-ACCT-1042); transaction membership not verified

UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: account_external_ids - customer-declared write-set member (registry ID FIC-REG-004821 and enterprise-entity mapping EC-004821 on both records); uniqueness constraints and transaction membership not verified
UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: account_merge_history - customer-declared append-only write-set member; append-only enforcement and transaction membership not verified
UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: audit_events - customer-declared write-set member; event content and transaction membership not verified
UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: transactional_outbox - customer-declared write-set member (outbox insertion required in the same transaction); event schema, ordering and transaction membership not verified

UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: CRM search index update by an outbox consumer - customer-declared asynchronous effect after commit, outside the database transaction; consumer idempotency, ordering and reconciliation not verified

UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: Billing customer read model update by an outbox consumer - customer-declared asynchronous effect after commit, outside the database transaction; consumer idempotency, ordering and reconciliation not verified

UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: ERP customer crosswalk update by an outbox consumer - customer-declared asynchronous effect after commit, outside the database transaction; consumer idempotency, ordering and reconciliation not verified

UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: storage of historical legal names and provenance needed for the adopt-current-name and preserve-history requirement - no table or column declared; may sit in accounts, account_external_ids, account_merge_history or an undeclared store
UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: disposition of source record CRM-ACCT-2097 (status flag, tombstone, redirect or retention) and its external IDs - mechanism and affected tables not declared
UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: historical activity records that must retain original account IDs - no table declared; foreign-key actions (for example cascading updates), triggers and rewrite risk not assessed

UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: undeclared dependents that may reference either account ID (contracts, subscriptions, billing or invoice records, tickets, ownership and permissions, reporting copies) - existence and foreign-key or trigger behaviour not assessed
UNKNOWN_UNVERIFIED: other write paths touching these tables during the operation (triggers, change-data-capture or replication consumers, other services) - not assessed
operations.temporal_scope: Legal-name change effective 2024-04-01; registry extract dated 2026-10-15; continuity must hold from creation of CRM-ACCT-1042 (2019-06-12) through the commit time; evidence currency window not defined by policy
operations.persistence_point: unknown / unverified - HOLD before first persistent write. Customer requirement: one PostgreSQL 16.5 SERIALIZABLE transaction, coordinated by MergeCoordinator 2.8.0, covering all writes to the seven declared tables and the outbox insertion, with the exact commit point being the COMMIT of that single transaction. The transaction boundary, its complete scope and the exact commit point are not evidenced. Outbox consumers (search index, Billing read model, ERP crosswalk) run after commit, outside the transaction.
operations.reversibility_basis: No recovery or compensation mechanism (A1), recovery test (A2) or customer attestation (A3) was supplied, and no positive technical evidence of irreversibility was supplied. Absence of evidence does not prove irreversibility, so factual reversibility remains unknown. The action class is the protected IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE path because a production MERGE changes shared identity state and feeds downstream consumers.
operations.classification_note: Mutation type MERGE is stated by the customer. IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE is the protected authorization class for a potentially shared production identity effect; it does not assert that technical recovery is impossible.

controls.title: Operation, scope and action-class binding
controls.trigger: Any request to execute OP-DEMO-2026-001 or any change to its source, target, direction, canonical record or effect scope.
controls.required_action: Before evidence evaluation and again immediately before the first persistent write, verify and record that the request is exactly MERGE of source CRM-ACCT-2097 into canonical CRM-ACCT-1042 (policy retains CRM-ACCT-1042), classified on the protected IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE path, with operation ID OP-DEMO-2026-001, idempotency key demo-merge-1042-2097-v1 and the declared effect scope. The agent or planner must not weaken, substitute or expand the required propositions or the effect scope. Any difference in direction, record IDs, canonical choice, added accounts or write-set members requires a new operation and fresh authorization.
controls.enforcement_point: Pre-persistence: MergeCoordinator request intake and the commit-boundary guard, before any approval request and again immediately before the first persistent write.
required_evidence: Operation request record bound to OP-DEMO-2026-001
Declared effect scope (write set and out-of-transaction effects)
Retain-canonical rule from POL-MDM-07 v3.2
controls.approval_requirement: None at this control; separate human approvals are required by CTRL-05.
controls.on_sufficient_support: Continue to the remaining controls; this control alone never authorizes the write.
controls.on_conflict: Block the request and require a new operation ID and fresh evaluation.
controls.on_indeterminate: HOLD; an unclassifiable or ambiguous effect class is treated as protected.
controls.on_failure: Fail closed: begin no persistent write and record the rejection in the audit trail.

controls.title: Registry-ID and legal-continuity identity gate (including negative control)
controls.trigger: Any proposal to treat two CRM accounts as one identity.
controls.required_action: Require for each candidate an exact official registry ID that matches the authoritative registry record, and separate evidence of legal continuity (a name change without dissolution, successor or new incorporation) applicable to the interval in scope. Names, domains, addresses and contact similarity are context only and never satisfy the gate. Candidates whose official registry IDs differ must not be merged regardless of similarity; the supplied policy defines no exception route, so an exception request is held for a customer policy decision.
controls.enforcement_point: Pre-persistence: evidence gate in the commit-boundary guard, before approval requests.
required_evidence: Official registry ID confirmed against the authoritative registry for each candidate
Evidence of legal continuity for the validity interval in scope
Recorded context-only treatment of name, domain, address and contact similarity
controls.on_sufficient_support: Pass this gate only; continue to CTRL-03 through CTRL-12.
controls.on_conflict: Registry IDs differ or continuity is contradicted: block the merge; route any exception request to the customer policy owner.
controls.on_indeterminate: Registry ID or continuity evidence missing or unverified: HOLD and request evidence; similarity is not a substitute.
controls.on_failure: Fail closed: no promotion of the identity claim and no write.
controls.owner: Data Steward (per POL-MDM-07 role); policy owner unassigned

controls.title: Evidence eligibility: provenance, independence and temporal applicability
controls.trigger: Any evidence item offered for the identity-continuity proposition.
controls.required_action: Admit each item first to quarantine, check admission conflicts, and promote only claim-specific eligible evidence with recorded source, proposition, evidentiary role (support, contradiction or unresolved), temporal applicability, validation basis, and validator and policy version. Do not count records that share an upstream origin (the migration report and the crosswalk) as independent proof. Treat a supplied signature-verification result as authentication of its source document only, not as separate identity evidence. Do not rely on planner confidence, repetition, an agent-generated verified label, or the absence of a detected conflict as support.
controls.enforcement_point: Pre-persistence: evidence admission and promotion service feeding the commit-boundary guard.
required_evidence: Source and provenance record for each item
Validator identity and version, and the policy that makes the item eligible
Temporal applicability against the validity interval and a customer-defined currency window
Dependency map showing shared upstream origins
controls.approval_requirement: Evidence eligibility rules are a customer policy decision (see GAP-02).
controls.on_sufficient_support: Eligible evidence is recorded per proposition and passed to the conflict check.
controls.on_conflict: Contested items stay quarantined for policy-designated adjudication.
controls.on_indeterminate: Unverified, stale or non-independent items are not authorization-eligible: HOLD or refresh.
controls.on_failure: Validator unavailable or promotion record missing: fail closed.

controls.title: Claim-specific conflict and indeterminate-evidence handling
controls.trigger: Evaluation of the identity-continuity proposition and again at the commit boundary.
controls.required_action: Run a claim-specific conflict check across eligible, active-unverified and quarantined evidence. Clear only when no unresolved material conflict remains. A contradiction (for example dissolution, a successor entity, a different registration number or a new incorporation) blocks the merge; indeterminate or unverified evidence blocks commit and routes to human adjudication. Absence of a detected conflict is never positive support.
controls.enforcement_point: Pre-persistence: conflict check in the commit-boundary guard.
required_evidence: Conflict-check result with evidence record IDs
Adjudication record when a conflict or indeterminate result occurs
controls.approval_requirement: Adjudication authority is a customer decision (see GAP-02).
controls.on_sufficient_support: Conflict status clear: continue to remaining controls.
controls.on_conflict: Block the merge and retain the conflict for adjudication.
controls.on_indeterminate: Block commit and route to human adjudication; do not treat as clear.

controls.title: Separate human approvals bound to the exact operation and state
controls.trigger: A request for commit authorization of OP-DEMO-2026-001.
controls.required_action: Require two separate human approvals, one from a Data Steward and one from a CRM Platform Owner, each bound to OP-DEMO-2026-001, the exact operation (MERGE of CRM-ACCT-2097 into CRM-ACCT-1042), idempotency key demo-merge-1042-2097-v1, source and canonical row versions (23 and 18), POL-MDM-07 v3.2, pre-commit validator 1.6 and the eligible-evidence record IDs. An approval is invalid if any bound element changes, if it is issued by an unauthorized or non-human principal, or if it precedes satisfaction of the evidence and write-set gates. No approval artifacts are currently supplied.
controls.enforcement_point: Pre-persistence: approval service and commit-boundary guard, rechecked at the commit boundary.
required_evidence: Data Steward approval record
CRM Platform Owner approval record
Binding fields (operation, key, row versions, policy and validator versions, evidence record IDs)
controls.approval_requirement: Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner, separately; whether one person may hold both roles is not stated (see GAP-01).
controls.on_sufficient_support: Approval gate passes; the commit still requires every other control.
controls.on_conflict: A reviewer records a conflict: HOLD and return to evidence adjudication.
controls.on_indeterminate: Approval missing, incomplete or unbound: HOLD.
controls.on_failure: Fail closed: no write without both valid approvals.
controls.owner: Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner (approvers); approval service owner unassigned

controls.title: Version binding and stale-state check
controls.trigger: Authorization time and again at the commit boundary.
controls.required_action: Bind and recheck source row version 23, canonical row version 18, POL-MDM-07 v3.2, pre-commit validator 1.6, identity schema CRM-IDENTITY-5 and the evidence eligibility state. Use compare-and-set or equivalent predicates on both account rows and on the link sets being re-pointed. Reject a stale authorization and re-evaluate from the beginning with a new authorization record (no replay) within one common retry budget. The SERIALIZABLE requirement is a customer requirement; whether it is sufficient against stale reads, lost updates, write skew and phantoms on the link sets needs database-specific design review, and isolation is assessed separately from atomicity.
controls.enforcement_point: Pre-persistence: commit-boundary guard and persistence adapter, at authorization and at the commit boundary.
required_evidence: Version snapshot recorded at authorization
Current-version snapshot at the commit boundary
Customer-defined retry budget
controls.approval_requirement: Re-approval is required when a bound version changes.
controls.on_conflict: A bound version changed or a competing change is detected: reject the authorization and re-evaluate.
controls.on_indeterminate: Versions cannot be read or compared: HOLD.
controls.on_failure: Fail closed; no replay of the stale candidate.

controls.title: Pre-write HOLD until write-set completeness and atomicity are proven
controls.trigger: Before the first persistent write of OP-DEMO-2026-001.
controls.required_action: Require customer-verified evidence that (a) the persistent write set is complete: the seven declared tables plus every dependent record, foreign-key action, trigger, historical-name store and source-record disposition; (b) all database writes and the outbox insertion occur in one identified PostgreSQL transaction with an identified exact commit point; and (c) external and asynchronous effects are inventoried. Otherwise HOLD: begin no partial sequence of writes and do not rely on later rollback. Atomicity is not inferred from a database product, an isolation level or a sequence of application calls.
controls.enforcement_point: Pre-persistence: MergeCoordinator readiness gate, before the transaction begins.
required_evidence: Verified write-set inventory
Evidence identifying the transaction, its scope and the exact commit point
Inventory of asynchronous and external effects
controls.approval_requirement: Customer sign-off on the inventory (see GAP-03 and GAP-04).
controls.on_sufficient_support: Inventory and atomicity verified: continue to the remaining controls.
controls.on_conflict: An undeclared dependent or a second commit is found: HOLD and correct the inventory.
controls.on_indeterminate: Unknown or unverified boundary or inventory: HOLD.
controls.owner: CRM Platform Owner (inventory sign-off role; owner assignment unconfirmed)

controls.title: Pre-commit invariant validation and transaction abort
controls.trigger: After the merge writes are applied inside the transaction and before COMMIT.
controls.required_action: Evaluate the invariants and abort the whole transaction if any fails: the realized operation equals the authorized scope; the canonical record remains CRM-ACCT-1042; the current legal name is adopted with historical names and provenance preserved; account_merge_history is append-only (no update or delete); historical activity keeps original account IDs; source contract links are re-pointed so that no active contract is lost (inference from supplied counts: eight active contract links on the canonical record, subject to the confirmed inventory); contact links follow an approved duplicate rule; registry-ID and external-ID uniqueness holds; audit and outbox rows are present; bound versions are still valid. On abort, confirm that none of the transaction's writes are visible.
controls.enforcement_point: Pre-commit: pre-commit validator 1.6 evaluated inside the same transaction and snapshot (to be confirmed by the customer), before COMMIT.
required_evidence: Invariant list and validator results
Same-snapshot evaluation evidence
controls.on_sufficient_support: All invariants pass: COMMIT is permitted subject to every other control.
controls.on_indeterminate: Validator result unknown or unavailable: abort and hold.
controls.on_failure: Abort the transaction (not a post-commit compensation) and confirm that no writes committed.

controls.title: Post-commit validation and downstream reconciliation
controls.required_action: Read authoritative state and compare it with the authorized effect (adopted name, historical names, link counts, merge-history, audit and outbox rows). Track each outbox event through the CRM search-index, Billing customer read-model and ERP customer-crosswalk consumers with idempotent, replay-safe processing, and reconcile each against authoritative state; report divergence. Consumer updates happen outside the database transaction and must not be described as covered by it.
controls.enforcement_point: Post-commit: reconciliation service and outbox consumers.
required_evidence: Post-commit state comparison
Per-consumer reconciliation records
controls.on_sufficient_support: Post-commit validation and reconciliation complete: record closure.
controls.on_indeterminate: Reconciliation incomplete: keep the operation open and further dependent changes on HOLD.

controls.title: Post-commit and out-of-boundary failure handling
controls.trigger: An invariant failure or consumer failure detected after commit or outside the atomic boundary.
controls.required_action: Stop dependent mutations, including further merges that involve either account; reconcile the actual persisted state; and apply only a documented, tested, operation-specific compensation or recovery procedure. If none is established, quarantine the affected records and events and escalate to the designated owner, keeping the overall decision on HOLD for further changes. Do not claim that a database rollback reverses committed or external effects; do not treat another operation as recovery unless it independently satisfies A1, A2 and A3.
controls.enforcement_point: Post-commit: reconciliation and recovery service; incident escalation path.
required_evidence: Reconciled state record
Documented and tested same-operation compensation procedure, if one exists
controls.approval_requirement: Recovery owner approval per customer policy (see GAP-07).
controls.on_sufficient_support: Recovered state is verified by reconciliation: close the incident.
controls.on_conflict: Persisted state conflicts with the authorization: quarantine and escalate.
controls.on_indeterminate: State cannot be established: quarantine and escalate.
controls.on_failure: Quarantine and escalate; no assumed rollback.

controls.title: Ambiguous commit outcome and idempotency
controls.trigger: A timeout, connection loss or other failure that leaves the commit outcome uncertain, or a repeated request.
controls.required_action: Persist and enforce idempotency key demo-merge-1042-2097-v1 (or an equivalent operation identifier) with the operation record. On an ambiguous commit outcome, do not retry; first reconcile authoritative state using the key and a read-after-failure check of the account rows, merge history, audit and outbox rows. Retry only after confirming that the original operation did not commit and that retry is safe, under the common retry budget and with fresh authorization when the snapshot changed. A duplicate request with the same key after a successful commit returns the recorded outcome and performs no second merge.
controls.enforcement_point: Cross-phase: MergeCoordinator outcome handler and persistence adapter.
required_evidence: Idempotency key record
Read-after-failure reconciliation result
controls.on_sufficient_support: Outcome established: proceed according to the established state.
controls.on_conflict: Reconciliation finds a conflicting or partial state: quarantine and escalate.
controls.on_indeterminate: Outcome cannot be established: no retry; HOLD and escalate.

controls.title: Reversibility and authorization-path gate (Path A or Path B)
controls.trigger: A request for commit authorization of OP-DEMO-2026-001.
controls.required_action: Treat OP-DEMO-2026-001 as IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE with factual reversibility unknown, and HOLD unless exactly one authorization path is established. Path A: A1 a documented recovery or compensation mechanism for this exact operation covering the complete production effect scope; A2 successful recovery tests on materially equivalent state and schema at current persistence, policy and validator versions; A3 attestation by a customer-designated responsible role. Path B (only when Path A is not established): a current explicit customer policy accepting this exact operation's non-recovery risk, operation-specific approval by an authorized role, and customer-defined separation of duties. Path A changes factual reversibility only; neither path changes the action class or replaces CTRL-01 through CTRL-11. Ordinary Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner approval does not count as acceptance of non-recovery risk. After Path A is established for the complete scope, Path B is unavailable for that scope. Path A eligibility expires on relevant version or scope drift, or when A2 or A3 goes stale.
controls.enforcement_point: Pre-persistence: authorization-path registry consulted by the commit-boundary guard.
required_evidence: A1 mechanism reference, A2 test records and A3 attestation (Path A)
Path B policy reference, operation-specific approval and separation-of-duties rule (Path B)
controls.approval_requirement: Path B approval role, A3 attester and separation-of-duties rule are customer decisions (see GAP-05).
controls.on_sufficient_support: One path established for the exact operation and scope: the gate passes; every other control still applies.
controls.on_conflict: Evidence shows both paths claimed for the same scope: block and resolve under customer policy.
controls.on_indeterminate: Neither path established or evidence stale: HOLD.

evidence_requirements.claim: CRM-ACCT-2097 and CRM-ACCT-1042 denote the same continuing legal person: the legal name changed on 2024-04-01 and the registration number and legal-person continuity are unchanged, with no dissolution, successor or new incorporation.
required_categories: Authoritative registry evidence of the registration and of continuity across the name change
Authentication of that registry evidence by a customer-designated validator
Independent corroboration where customer policy requires it
source_characteristics: Issued by the authoritative registry and identifying the registration number
Authenticated with recorded validator identity and version
Independent of the CRM systems and of the migration that created the duplicate
Directly stating continuity, not inferred from similarity
evidence_requirements.temporal_applicability: Must cover the name change on 2024-04-01 and continuity from creation of CRM-ACCT-1042 (2019-06-12) through the commit time; the extract is dated 2026-10-15 and no currency window is defined.
evidence_requirements.validation_method: Customer-defined: authoritative registry lookup or authenticated extract, with a promotion record naming the policy and validator version. Not performed by the Planner.
evidence_requirements.conflict_handling: Any evidence of dissolution, successor entity, different registration number or new incorporation is a contradiction that blocks the merge and goes to Data Steward adjudication.
evidence_requirements.unverified_handling: Keep unverified or quarantined items distinct from authorization-eligible evidence; do not treat them as support.

Promotion eligibility has not been decided by the customer

required_categories: Registry ID attribute on each candidate record
Authoritative registry record showing the same registration number
source_characteristics: Registry ID read from the authoritative registry, not only copied between CRM records
Exact match, not fuzzy or partial
evidence_requirements.temporal_applicability: Current at evaluation time and at the commit boundary.

evidence_requirements.conflict_handling: A mismatch or a different registry ID for either candidate blocks the merge (negative control).
evidence_requirements.unverified_handling: A registry ID appearing only in CRM fields is a candidate attribute, not verified identity evidence.
evidence_requirements.policy_owner: unassigned (MDM policy owner for POL-MDM-07 not identified)

evidence_requirements.claim: The name-change continuity claim applies to the relevant referent and validity interval: the change took effect on 2024-04-01, before the source record was created on 2024-05-15, and continuity still holds at the time of commit.
required_categories: Registry statement of the effective date of the name change
Evidence currency relative to the commit time
Link between each CRM record's creation date and the pre-change or post-change name
source_characteristics: Dated, with a customer-defined currency window
evidence_requirements.temporal_applicability: Interval from 2019-06-12 (creation of CRM-ACCT-1042) through the commit time, including 2024-04-01 and 2024-05-15.
evidence_requirements.validation_method: Customer-defined comparison of the extract date and effective date with policy; recheck at the commit boundary.
evidence_requirements.conflict_handling: Defer if temporal applicability or legal continuity is unresolved.
evidence_requirements.unverified_handling: Stale or undated evidence is not authorization-eligible.
evidence_requirements.policy_owner: unassigned (MDM policy owner for POL-MDM-07 not identified)
gaps: No statement that the legal agreement of 2025-02-14 is linked to either CRM account

evidence_requirements.claim: Evidence items count as independent corroboration only when they do not share an upstream origin; the migration report and the crosswalk form one dependency cluster and are not independent identity proof.
source_characteristics: Separate origin from the CRM migration
Not produced or induced by the merge hypothesis
evidence_requirements.temporal_applicability: Origin and creation dates of the migration report (2024-05-15) and the crosswalk.
evidence_requirements.validation_method: Customer-defined dependency analysis recorded with the promotion decision.
evidence_requirements.conflict_handling: Do not promote a mapping solely because the planner hypothesis induced the retrieval or the mapping.
evidence_requirements.unverified_handling: Keep both items as context in the active set; neither counts as independent support.
evidence_requirements.policy_owner: unassigned (MDM policy owner for POL-MDM-07 not identified)
gaps: The derivation of the crosswalk from the migration report is not described

evidence_requirements.claim: Two related companies with different official registry IDs are not the same legal person and must not be merged merely because names, domain, address or contacts are similar (negative control).
required_categories: Official registry ID of each company from the authoritative registry
evidence_requirements.validation_method: Exact registry-ID comparison before any similarity is considered.

evidence_requirements.unverified_handling: Similarity evidence is context only and is never promoted as identity support.
evidence_requirements.policy_owner: unassigned (MDM policy owner for POL-MDM-07 not identified)
gaps: Exception process, if any, is undefined

required_categories: A1 mechanism, A2 test records and A3 attestation for Path A
Current policy, operation-specific approval and separation-of-duties rule for Path B

gaps: No A1, A2 or A3 evidence supplied
No Path B policy, approver or separation-of-duties rule supplied
Path A and Path B are Skill-level planning constraints; the reference contract retrieved here defines the protected authorization phases, not these paths

Issued after the evidence gate and bound to current versions

evidence_requirements.conflict_handling: Changed binding or conflicting reviewer finding: HOLD.

Inventory of asynchronous and external effects

evidence_requirements.conflict_handling: Any undeclared effect or second commit: HOLD.

Transaction membership and commit point are not evidenced

implementation_points.responsibility: Customer-declared coordinator of the merge: receive the request, bind operation and scope, sequence the controls and the single transaction.
Customer-declared service that reported signature and issuer-certificate verification of the registry extract; supply validator identity and version to the promotion record.

implementation_points.responsibility: Quarantine admission, conflict check and claim-specific promotion with recorded provenance, role, temporal applicability and validator version.
Evaluate the registry-ID and continuity rules, retain-canonical rule and name-adoption rule against eligible evidence.
Collect and validate separate Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner approvals bound to the exact operation and state.

implementation_points.responsibility: Customer-declared validator; confirm that it can evaluate the listed invariants inside the same transaction and snapshot before COMMIT.
Verify operation, scope, evidence, conflicts, approvals, versions, write-set and atomicity proof and authorization path before the first write and at the commit boundary; fail closed.
inputs: Path A or Path B record
outputs: Allow or HOLD decision with reasons

implementation_points.responsibility: Customer-declared single SERIALIZABLE transaction over the declared tables and outbox insertion; identify the exact commit point; compare-and-set on row versions.

Post-commit validation, ambiguous-commit reconciliation by idempotency key, downstream reconciliation, quarantine and escalation.

Hold A1, A2 and A3 evidence and the Path B policy, approval and separation-of-duties records, with version-drift expiry.

outputs: Path A or Path B eligibility with expiry

validation_tests.scenario: Sufficient support under policy (hypothetical positive)
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. Both candidates carry the same official registry ID confirmed against the authoritative registry; an authenticated, currently applicable registry extract states a legal-name change on 2024-04-01 with unchanged registration number and continuity and no dissolution, successor or new incorporation; the validator, policy version and promotion record are recorded; no conflicting evidence exists in eligible, active or quarantined sets.
validation_tests.action: Submit the proposed MERGE OP-DEMO-2026-001 to the evidence gate (registry-ID and continuity gate, evidence eligibility and conflict check).
validation_tests.expected_result: The gate records support with a clear conflict status and per-proposition evidence record IDs. The result does not authorize the operation: approvals, version binding, write-set and atomicity proof, and the authorization-path gate all still apply.

validation_tests.scenario: Negative control: related companies with different official registry IDs
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. A synthetic pair of related companies (for example parent and subsidiary) with similar names, the same domain, the same address and overlapping contacts, but different official registry IDs, each confirmed by the authoritative registry.
validation_tests.action: Propose a MERGE of the synthetic pair through the same gate that evaluates OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: The exact registry-ID requirement fails. Name, domain, address and contact similarity is recorded as context only. No merge authorization can be produced and the request is held with no write started. Any exception request is routed to a customer policy decision because the supplied policy defines no exception route.

validation_tests.scenario: Same registry ID but no legal-continuity evidence
validation_tests.setup: Both candidates carry the same registry ID; only name, domain and address similarity and internal mappings are available; no registry extract or equivalent continuity evidence is supplied.
validation_tests.action: Submit OP-DEMO-2026-001 to the evidence gate.
validation_tests.expected_result: Required positive support is missing: HOLD, no promotion of the internal mappings as identity proof, and a request for continuity evidence. Similarity is not accepted as a substitute.

validation_tests.scenario: Non-independent corroboration (shared upstream origin)
validation_tests.setup: The only corroboration for the identity claim is the migration report and the crosswalk that both map the two CRM IDs to one enterprise-entity code, plus the matching registry-ID field copied into both CRM records.
validation_tests.action: Submit OP-DEMO-2026-001 to the evidence gate with no registry-origin evidence.
validation_tests.expected_result: The migration report and crosswalk are treated as one dependency cluster and are not counted as independent identity proof; the claim stays unsupported and the request is held.

validation_tests.scenario: Material contradiction in registry evidence
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. The registry evidence shows a different registration number for one candidate, or records a dissolution, a successor entity or a new incorporation that reuses the trading name.
validation_tests.action: Submit OP-DEMO-2026-001 to the evidence gate.
validation_tests.expected_result: A material contradiction is established: the merge is blocked, the conflict is retained for Data Steward adjudication, and no write begins. The planner cannot override or weaken the finding.

validation_tests.scenario: Unverified or indeterminate evidence (verification absent, failed or validator unavailable)
validation_tests.setup: The signature and issuer-certificate verification result for the registry extract is absent, failed, from an unidentified validator, or the evidence gateway is unavailable.
validation_tests.action: Submit OP-DEMO-2026-001 to the evidence gate.
validation_tests.expected_result: The extract stays quarantined or unverified, is not authorization-eligible, and the request is held (fail closed). An unverified item is not treated as clear.

validation_tests.scenario: Temporal mismatch or stale registry evidence
validation_tests.setup: The registry extract is older than the customer-defined currency window, or does not cover the 2024-04-01 name change and the validity interval in scope.
validation_tests.action: Submit OP-DEMO-2026-001 to the evidence gate.
validation_tests.expected_result: Temporal applicability fails: HOLD, refresh the evidence, and re-evaluate with a new authorization record.

validation_tests.scenario: Wrong operation scope, direction or canonical record
validation_tests.setup: The request is altered so that it merges CRM-ACCT-1042 into CRM-ACCT-2097, adds a third account, or names a canonical record other than CRM-ACCT-1042, contrary to the retain-canonical rule.
validation_tests.action: Submit the altered request to the operation and scope binding check for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: The request is blocked; a new operation ID and fresh evaluation are required; no write begins.

validation_tests.scenario: Only one of the two required approvals
validation_tests.setup: Evidence and write-set gates are satisfied in a fixture; only the Data Steward approval exists (then repeat with only the CRM Platform Owner approval).
validation_tests.action: Request commit authorization for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: HOLD in both variants: both separate human approvals are required and neither substitutes for the other.

validation_tests.scenario: Approvals bound to a different operation or state
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. Both approvals exist but are bound to a different operation ID, a different idempotency key, row versions other than 18 and 23, or a different policy version.
validation_tests.action: Request commit authorization for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: The approvals are invalid for this operation and state: HOLD and request new approvals bound to the exact operation and state.

validation_tests.scenario: Valid bound approvals (hypothetical positive)
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner approvals are issued by principals authorized for those roles, are human, and are bound to OP-DEMO-2026-001, its idempotency key, row versions 18 and 23, the policy version and the evidence record IDs.
validation_tests.action: Request commit authorization for OP-DEMO-2026-001 after the evidence gate has passed.
validation_tests.expected_result: The approval gate passes only. The commit still requires version binding, write-set and atomicity proof, pre-commit invariants and the authorization-path gate.

validation_tests.scenario: Stale row version between approval and commit
validation_tests.setup: After approval, the canonical row version changes from 18 to 19, or the source row version from 23 to 24, before the commit boundary.
validation_tests.action: Attempt to commit OP-DEMO-2026-001 with the existing authorization.
validation_tests.expected_result: The authorization is rejected as stale; the stale candidate is not replayed; evaluation restarts from the beginning with a new authorization record within the common retry budget.

validation_tests.scenario: Policy, validator or schema version drift
validation_tests.setup: After approval, the policy version moves from POL-MDM-07 v3.2, or the pre-commit validator from 1.6, or the identity schema from CRM-IDENTITY-5.
validation_tests.action: Attempt to commit OP-DEMO-2026-001 with the existing authorization.
validation_tests.expected_result: The authorization is stale: HOLD and re-evaluate against the current versions; no replay of the earlier decision.

validation_tests.scenario: Write-set completeness unverified before first write
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. Review finds a dependent table, foreign-key action or trigger that references either account but is outside the seven declared tables.
validation_tests.action: Request the pre-write readiness check for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: HOLD before the first persistent write; no partial sequence of writes begins; the inventory is corrected and re-reviewed before any retry.

validation_tests.scenario: Atomicity unverified before first write
validation_tests.setup: Evidence cannot show that all database writes and the outbox insertion occur in one identified transaction with a single commit point (for example the outbox insert is issued separately, or more than one commit is used).
validation_tests.action: Request the pre-write readiness check for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: HOLD; no reliance on later rollback; the SERIALIZABLE setting is not accepted as proof of atomicity; database-specific design review is required.

validation_tests.scenario: Pre-commit invariant failure inside a verified atomic transaction
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. Atomicity is verified for the fixture. The validator then detects a violated invariant, such as an update to account_merge_history, a lost contract link, or missing historical-name preservation.
validation_tests.action: Run the pre-commit invariant validation for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: The whole transaction is aborted; none of the transaction's writes, including audit and outbox rows, are committed; the rejection is recorded outside the aborted transaction; no event is published.

validation_tests.scenario: Serialization failure (definite abort) under the SERIALIZABLE requirement
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. A concurrent transaction causes the database to report a serialization failure for the merge transaction.
validation_tests.action: Execute the fixture transaction for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: The transaction is rolled back with no partial effects; the stale candidate is not replayed; evaluation restarts from a fresh snapshot with a new authorization record within the common retry budget; when the budget is exhausted the request is held and escalated.

validation_tests.scenario: Post-commit validation failure
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. After commit, read-after-commit validation finds a divergence from the authorized effect (for example link counts or the adopted legal name).
validation_tests.action: Run post-commit validation for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: Dependent mutations stop; actual persisted state is reconciled; only a documented, tested compensation for this exact operation may be used, otherwise affected records and events are quarantined and escalated; no claim that rollback undoes the commit.

validation_tests.scenario: Consumer failure and duplicate events outside the database transaction
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. The ERP crosswalk consumer times out and the search-index consumer receives the same outbox event twice.
validation_tests.action: Process the outbox events for OP-DEMO-2026-001 and run downstream reconciliation.
validation_tests.expected_result: Consumers are idempotent (no double apply); failed deliveries are retried from the outbox; reconciliation reports divergence against authoritative state; the database merge is not re-executed and the Billing read model is not reported complete until reconciled.

validation_tests.scenario: Ambiguous commit outcome
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. The connection is lost while the COMMIT of the merge transaction is in flight.
validation_tests.action: Handle the failure for OP-DEMO-2026-001 under key demo-merge-1042-2097-v1.
validation_tests.expected_result: No blind retry. Authoritative state is read back using the idempotency key (account rows, merge history, audit and outbox rows). A retry occurs only after confirming the original did not commit and retry is safe; if it did commit, post-commit validation and consumer reconciliation proceed instead.

validation_tests.scenario: Duplicate request and idempotency key reuse
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. The operation already committed under key demo-merge-1042-2097-v1; the same request is submitted again, and separately a request with the same key but different content is submitted.
validation_tests.action: Submit both requests for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: The identical request returns the recorded outcome with no second merge and no duplicate outbox event; the same key with different content is rejected.

validation_tests.scenario: Preservation invariants (history, append-only, name adoption)
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. A merge fixture in which historical activity rows are touched, account_merge_history is updated or deleted, the current legal name is not adopted, or historical names and provenance are dropped.
validation_tests.action: Run pre-commit invariant validation for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: Each violation is detected and aborts the transaction; in the conforming fixture, historical activity keeps its original account IDs, merge history is append-only, the current legal name is adopted, and historical names and provenance are preserved.

validation_tests.scenario: Path A positive (hypothetical): A1, A2 and A3 established
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. A1: a documented recovery or compensation mechanism for this exact MERGE operation covers the complete production effect scope, including the downstream consumer effects. A2: successful recovery tests on materially equivalent state and schema at the current PostgreSQL, policy, validator and schema versions. A3: attestation by a customer-designated responsible role confirms A1 and A2 applicability and results. The write-set inventory is complete.
validation_tests.action: Evaluate the authorization path for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path A eligibility and factual reversibility reversible for the proven scope only; the action class stays IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE; all other controls still apply.

validation_tests.scenario: Path A negative A1: mechanism missing, wrong operation or incomplete scope
validation_tests.setup: A2 and A3 exist, but the documented recovery mechanism is absent, belongs to a different operation (for example a separate unmerge procedure not independently qualified), or does not cover the complete effect scope.
validation_tests.action: Evaluate the authorization path for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path A is not established: HOLD; factual reversibility remains unknown.

validation_tests.scenario: Path A negative A2: recovery test absent, failed, stale or not equivalent
validation_tests.setup: A1 and A3 exist, but recovery tests are absent, failed, stale, or run on non-equivalent state, schema or non-current persistence, policy or validator versions.
validation_tests.action: Evaluate the authorization path for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path A is not established: HOLD; factual reversibility remains unknown.

validation_tests.scenario: Path A negative A3: attestation absent, unauthorized or not covering A1/A2
validation_tests.setup: A1 and A2 exist, but the attestation is absent, signed by a role not designated by the customer, or does not attest A1 and A2 applicability and results.
validation_tests.action: Evaluate the authorization path for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path A is not established: HOLD; factual reversibility remains unknown.

validation_tests.scenario: Path B positive (hypothetical): explicit acceptance of non-recovery risk
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. Path A is not established. A current explicit customer policy accepts this exact operation's non-recovery risk; an authorized role gives operation-specific approval; the customer-defined separation of duties is satisfied.
validation_tests.action: Evaluate the authorization path for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path B eligibility only. The action class stays IRREVERSIBLE_WRITE and factual reversibility stays unknown; Path B does not demonstrate recoverability. All other controls still apply.

validation_tests.scenario: Path B negative policy: no current policy accepting this risk
validation_tests.setup: Path A is not established and approvals exist, but no current explicit policy accepts this exact operation's non-recovery risk.
validation_tests.action: Evaluate the authorization path for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: HOLD; Path B is unavailable.

validation_tests.scenario: Path B negative approval or authority
validation_tests.setup: A current policy exists, but operation-specific risk-acceptance approval is absent or given by a role the policy does not authorize; only the ordinary Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner merge approvals exist.
validation_tests.action: Evaluate the authorization path for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: HOLD; ordinary merge approval does not count as acceptance of non-recovery risk.

validation_tests.scenario: Path B negative separation of duties
validation_tests.setup: A current policy and an authorized approval exist, but separation of duties is undefined, unresolved or violated (for example the risk approver is the ordinary approver and the policy requires independence).
validation_tests.action: Evaluate the authorization path for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: HOLD; Path B is unavailable until separation of duties is resolved under customer policy.

validation_tests.scenario: Path exclusivity after Path A is established
validation_tests.setup: HYPOTHETICAL fixture, not customer evidence or policy. Path A is established for the complete effect scope of this operation.
validation_tests.action: Attempt to solicit or record non-recovery-risk acceptance (Path B) for OP-DEMO-2026-001.
validation_tests.expected_result: Path B is unavailable for that operation and scope; no risk acceptance is solicited or recorded. If A2 or A3 later goes stale or a relevant version drifts, Path A expires, factual reversibility returns to unknown, and HOLD applies until Path A is renewed or Path B is independently established.

planner_checks.scenario: Public reference MCP unavailable or materially incomplete
planner_checks.setup: A required public MCP retrieval is unavailable or a required response field is materially incomplete.
planner_checks.expected_result: Use degraded_reference_unavailable; mark affected claims unresolved; invent no reference-backed content or provenance.

planner_checks.scenario: Reference version drift within one run
planner_checks.setup: Two or more required retrievals in the same run expose incompatible reference-set versions.
planner_checks.action: Compare the version basis of each source and resolve the mismatch.
planner_checks.expected_result: Do not silently combine versions; refresh consistently or mark dependent decisions unresolved or degraded.

planner_checks.setup: The request is not an identity-changing entity-resolution operation (for example an ordinary field update).
planner_checks.action: Qualify the request against the Skill's scope.
planner_checks.expected_result: State the scope boundary; fabricate no operations, controls or reference coverage.

assumptions.statement: The evidence descriptions (registry extract, gateway result, agreement, migration report, crosswalk) accurately describe the underlying documents.
assumptions.basis: Customer-supplied task input; the Planner saw no source document.
assumptions.impact: If a description is inaccurate the support assessment may change or reverse.
assumptions.verification: Data Steward reviews the original documents, not the descriptions.

assumptions.statement: The architecture and write set (seven tables, one SERIALIZABLE transaction including outbox insertion, asynchronous consumers) are customer-declared requirements and are not verified implementation facts.
assumptions.impact: If the implementation differs, atomicity and write-set completeness fail and HOLD applies.
assumptions.verification: Customer verifies schema, coordinator behaviour and consumers (GAP-03, GAP-04).

assumptions.statement: The customer's premise that both CRM records may represent one legal person is a hypothesis to be tested, not a conclusion.
assumptions.impact: Treating it as established would bypass the evidence gate.
assumptions.verification: Evidence gate in CTRL-02 to CTRL-04.

assumptions.statement: The full text of POL-MDM-07 v3.2 matches the summary supplied; no exception route, evidence currency window or approver identities are defined.
assumptions.basis: Task input summarizes the policy; the document was not supplied.
assumptions.impact: A different policy may change evidence sufficiency or approval rules.
assumptions.verification: Policy owner confirms the summary and answers GAP-01 and GAP-02.

assumptions.statement: Source row version 23 and canonical row version 18 are the current versions at the time of the request and are re-read at authorization and at the commit boundary.
The enterprise-entity code EC-004821 and the registry ID FIC-REG-004821 are different identifiers; similarity of their digits is not treated as proof of equivalence.
assumptions.basis: Different prefixes and sources in the task input.
assumptions.impact: Treating them as equivalent could count an internal mapping as registry proof.

assumptions.statement: All case data are synthetic; this is a planning exercise with no production access, database write, deployment or real authorization.
assumptions.impact: None for a synthetic case; a real run would need production-safe handling.

assumptions.statement: Operation ID OP-DEMO-2026-001 and idempotency key demo-merge-1042-2097-v1 are intended for this exact operation only.
assumptions.impact: Reuse for a different operation would defeat idempotency and binding.

assumptions.statement: Arguments sent to the public reference service in this run contained only abstract labels (action class, mutation type, entity class, observation domain, temporal scope, include flags).
assumptions.basis: The submitted arguments were inspected in this run.
assumptions.impact: A leak would be a privacy breach of customer information.
assumptions.verification: Review the recorded call arguments listed in the README.

unresolved_decisions.question: No approval artifacts were supplied. Who are the authorized Data Steward and CRM Platform Owner, what binding format and expiry apply, and may one person hold both roles?
unresolved_decisions.impact: No commit authorization is possible without both separate, bound human approvals.

unresolved_decisions.question: Who or what designates the registry extract and the supplied gateway result as authorization-eligible; which validator and version; what evidence currency window applies; is one authoritative source sufficient; and does the actual extract state the registration number and the old and new legal names?
unresolved_decisions.impact: Evidence supports the proposition on its description only; it is not authorization-eligible until promoted under a defined policy.
unresolved_decisions.owner: Customer MDM policy owner and Data Steward

unresolved_decisions.question: What is the complete persistent write set? Confirm dependent tables, foreign-key actions and triggers, where historical legal names and provenance are stored, the disposition of the source record, contact-link duplicate handling, uniqueness constraints and where historical activity keeps original account IDs.
unresolved_decisions.impact: Write-set completeness is unverified; HOLD applies before the first persistent write.

unresolved_decisions.question: What evidence shows that all database writes and the outbox insertion run in one PostgreSQL transaction with an identified commit point, that pre-commit validator 1.6 can evaluate invariants in the same snapshot before COMMIT, and that SERIALIZABLE is adequate for the link-set anomalies?
unresolved_decisions.impact: Atomicity is unverified; no reliance on rollback is permitted.

limitations: Design-time plan only: no controls were deployed, no runtime authorization was performed, no database was accessed and no customer data was changed.
All evidence is customer-supplied description; the Planner verified nothing and declares no evidence verified or authorization-eligible.
The architecture, write set and policy are customer-declared requirements, not verified implementation facts; write-set completeness and atomicity are unverified.
No approval artifacts exist and none is assumed; the operation is not authorized to commit.

Reference material returned by the public service is a non-executable reference; constraint examples are illustrative and mappings are non-normative; the service does not assess evidence or issue verdicts.
Path A and Path B are Skill-level planning constraints, not text of the retrieved reference contract.

No Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema engine, format checker or RFC 8785 implementation was available: schema validation, format validation and negative controls, and sidecar checks that depend on them were not run; the package is not fully validated.
Customer runtime tests, external-client compatibility and ZIP integrity were not run; all proposed validation tests and planner checks remain proposed.
Nothing here is legal advice or a legal-entity determination.

validation_record.validator: No compatible JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 engine was invoked. Supplementary helper: custom Python 3.12.3 script check.py (semantic/reference-integrity and Markdown/JSON consistency checker; it is not a JSON Schema validator).
notes: Environment discovery: Python 3.12.3 could not import jsonschema, fastjsonschema or jsonschema_rs; Node v22.23.5 provided only Ajv 6.15.0 (Draft-07 only; ajv/dist/2020 absent) and no ajv-formats. No package was installed, as instructed.

schema_validation, format_validation and format_checker_negative_control are not_run for that reason. JSON parsing was used only as a prerequisite and is not schema validation. Because these readiness-critical checks are unverified, the plan cannot be reported as validated.
No RFC 8785 (JCS) implementation was available in the environment; sidecar comparison S1 depends on one and is therefore expected to be not_run; no ad hoc serializer was substituted.

Five public MCP retrievals succeeded in this run (get_reference_status, get_mutation_guardrail_profile, get_evidence_promotion_contract, get_commit_boundary_contract for PHASE_1 and PHASE_2); the status and profile responses reported identical reference-set versions. The submitted arguments were inspected and contained only abstract labels.

Judgement checks (operation classification, authorization-path coverage, effect boundaries, MCP provenance interpretation) were performed manually and are recorded manual_pass. Mechanical checks were run by check.py.
All 31 customer-operation tests and 3 planner checks are proposed; none was executed. customer_runtime_tests, external_client_compatibility and zip_integrity were not run.
